Emit a cone $C$ from the camera projection center $\mathbf{o}$ along the direction $\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{p}_o - \mathbf{o}$, where $\mathbf{p}_o$ is the pixel center.

Determine a set of sampling distances $t_i$.
For each distance $t_i$, calculate the sphere center $\mathbf{x}_i$ and inscribed radius $r_i$.
The radius $r_i$ is calculated to ensure the sphere is inscribed within the cone.
Orthogonally project each sphere $S_i(\mathbf{x}_i, r_i)$ onto the three Tri-Mip planes (XY, YZ, XZ).
This step leverages the isotropic pre-filtering of the Tri-Mip encoding.
